inputs.proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.
inputs.original_proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.

questions: Are there any other QML or C++ files that still reference `Bridge.coreInitialized` or expect the `coreInitializedChanged` signal?
Will calling `ecuio_shutdown()` unconditionally in the destructor cause any issues if multiple `QtTuneBridge` instances are created and destroyed in quick succession?
Is there any code that relies on the return value of `ecuio_init()` being stored or checked elsewhere, now that it is ignored?
Could the removal of the `m_initialized` member affect any thread‑safety guarantees or the logic that ensures `ecuio_shutdown()` is only called after a successful `ecuio_init()`?
nits: Consider adding a comment in `QtTuneBridge` explaining that `ecuio_init()` is a no‑op and its return value is always `ECUIO_OK` to aid future maintainers.
If the `coreInitialized` property is still part of the public API, keep it as a read‑only property that always returns `true` to avoid breaking existing QML bindings.
